name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_STATEMENT4_Q01 - Synthetic methods and basic characteristics of amines

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the synthesis and basicity of amines:

Statement I: Reduction of nitriles with lithium aluminium hydride (\(\mathrm{LiAlH}_4\)) or catalytic hydrogenation yields primary amines containing one carbon atom more than the starting alkyl halide used to prepare the nitrile.

Statement II: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis readily produces high yields of pure aromatic primary amines like aniline.

Statement III: Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than ammonia in aqueous solution because alkyl groups possess a \(+I\) inductive effect.

Statement IV: Aniline is a weaker base than ammonia because the lone pair of electrons on nitrogen is delocalized over the aromatic ring through resonance.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The preparation and relative basicity of amines are dictated by carbon-chain transformations, nucleophilic substitution feasibility, and the electronic environment (inductive vs. resonance delocalization) of the nitrogen lone pair.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
The assertion that reduction of nitriles using \(\mathrm{LiAlH}_4\) or catalytic hydrogenation produces primary amines with an ascent of the series (incorporating the nitrile carbon) is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
The assertion that aromatic primary amines such as aniline can be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is incorrect because aryl halides fail to undergo bimolecular nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion under standard conditions.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement III
The assertion that aliphatic amines are stronger bases than ammonia in aqueous solution due to the electron-releasing \(+I\) effect of alkyl groups, which stabilizes the alkylammonium cation, is correct.

Step 5: Evaluation of Statement IV
The assertion that aniline is a weaker base than ammonia because its nitrogen lone pair enters into resonance conjugation with the benzene ring (rendering it less accessible for protonation) is correct.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Statements I, III, and IV are correct, whereas Statement II is incorrect. Concluding assessment: I, III and IV only are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_AMINES_STATEMENT4_Q02 - Chemical reactions and diazonium coupling of amines

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements regarding the reactions of amines and diazonium salts:

Statement I: Primary aliphatic and aromatic amines react with chloroform and ethanolic potassium hydroxide to produce intensely foul-smelling isocyanides.

Statement II: The product obtained from the reaction of a primary amine with benzenesulphonyl chloride contains an acidic hydrogen and dissolves in aqueous potassium hydroxide.

Statement III: Direct nitration of aniline with a nitrating mixture gives exclusively the ortho- and para-nitro derivatives without any meta-substituted product.

Statement IV: Coupling of benzenediazonium chloride with phenol in a weakly alkaline medium takes place at the para position to form \(p\)-hydroxyazobenzene.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Reactions of amines and diazonium salts encompass electrophilic substitutions, nucleophilic additions/eliminations, and azo coupling reactions dependent on medium acidity and resonance activation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
The assertion that primary aliphatic and aromatic amines undergo the carbylamine reaction upon heating with chloroform and ethanolic \(\mathrm{KOH}\) to form isocyanides is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
The assertion that the Hinsberg reaction of a primary amine yields an \(N\)-alkylbenzenesulphonamide with an acidic hydrogen on nitrogen that dissolves in aqueous \(\mathrm{KOH}\) is correct.

Step 4: Evaluation of Statement III
The assertion that direct nitration of aniline yields exclusively ortho- and para-products is incorrect because in strongly acidic media, aniline protonates to form the meta-directing anilinium ion, producing a significant yield (47%) of \(m\)-nitroaniline.

Step 5: Evaluation of Statement IV
The assertion that benzenediazonium chloride couples with phenol at the para position in mildly alkaline medium (pH 9–10) to generate the orange dye \(p\)-hydroxyazobenzene is correct.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Statements I, II, and IV are correct, whereas Statement III is incorrect. Concluding assessment: I, II and IV only are correct.
